label: D2 after a2->S2 (common) while policy already leans back toward a1
explanation: Fires only at D2, only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 through a common transition (in_action=2, in_state=2; 100% of activations). It never fires at D1 or GO, after a1, or on rare transitions. Within a2->S2c D2 steps it is selective for cases where the a2 choice is weakly supported: prev_reward==0 (96% of mass), and very often the choice was a switch from a1 after an unrewarded trial (stay==0 is 8.9x lift). The best single modulator is the model own policy logit at that D2 step: it fires when choice=logit(a1)-logit(a2) > 0, i.e. the policy already leans back toward a1 (dev P=0.59 R=0.82 F1=0.69 mass recall 0.93). Magnitude grows with choice: choice>1 gives precision 0.91 and covers 82% of the top quartile but only 18% of the bottom quartile. It does not fire when the policy strongly favours a2 (choice < -1.5) or when the previous trial was rewarded. Other predicates scored: a2&S2c alone (F1 0.09), adding prev_reward==0 (F1 0.21), adding the switch from a1 (F1 0.57), choice>0.5 (F1 0.73 but mass recall 0.82). I kept choice>0 because it is simpler and keeps more of the mass. Uses only observed inputs plus the model own output, so no future variables.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Lower it: common=0 (-4.53), action=1 (-3.98), in_action=1 (-3.98), choice_bin=decile 2 (9 = most a1) (-3.72).
